def: Describes a process that keeps producing outputs that are both novel and learnable to an observer, without a fixed end point.
Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer: an algorithm that evolves a population of environments together with the agents that solve them, and transfers agents between environments.
An ordering of tasks from easy to hard that lets a learner acquire skills it could not learn on the hard task alone.
A filter that admits a new environment only if the current agent scores neither too low to learn from nor too high to be worth learning.
A learning problem together with the agent being trained on it, the unit of population in POET.
Testing an agent from one environment on another and adopting it if it scores higher there, so skills spread between challenges.
A black-box optimiser that estimates a direction of improvement by scoring random perturbations of the parameters and moving toward the better ones.
Accumulated number of novel environments created and solved, a measure of whether a system keeps producing new solvable challenges.
The property that an observer who studies more of a process's history can predict its later outputs better.
An approach that aims to produce general intelligence by meta-learning architectures, learning algorithms and automatically generated environments.
A reward signal that is zero almost everywhere, so an optimiser gets no feedback until it is already close to success.
